subject: Polity
description: Chief Minister of Indian states — appointment, tenure, powers, oath, role vis-à-vis Governor and State Legislature, recent CM data points.

questions.stem: The Chief Minister of an Indian state is APPOINTED by:
questions.explanation: Article 164(1): 'The Chief Minister shall be appointed by the GOVERNOR.' Convention: the Governor invites the leader of the majority party (or coalition) in the LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY to form government. KEY DISTINCTIONS: (1) Governor's appointment is FORMAL — actual CM is decided by ELECTORAL VERDICT. (2) If no clear majority — Governor's DISCRETION matters; he/she may invite the largest single party or pre-poll alliance leader (refer Sarkaria, Punchhi Commission guidelines). (3) CM need not be an MLA at the time of appointment — but must become one within 6 MONTHS (Article 164(4)). FAMOUS CASES: Mamata Banerjee (West Bengal 2021) and Yogi Adityanath (UP 2017) were not MLAs when sworn in; both contested by-elections within 6 months. SAME PROVISION FOR PM: Article 75(1) — PM appointed by President, similar discretion. EXAM ANGLE: 'who appoints CM' is a 1-mark CGL/UPSC staple — appears in 50% of polity papers. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests basic federal-architecture knowledge — Governor as the constitutional head of state government.

questions.stem: What is the MAXIMUM time within which a Chief Minister must become a member of the State Legislature after appointment?

options.option_text: Six months from oath of office

questions.explanation: Article 164(4): 'A Minister who for any period of SIX consecutive months is not a member of the Legislature of the State shall at the expiration of that period cease to be a Minister.' This applies to the CM and all state ministers. PRECEDENT — S.R. CHAUDHURI v. STATE OF PUNJAB (2001): SC ruled that a non-member CANNOT be re-appointed minister after 6 months without first getting elected — closing a loophole used in Punjab where Tej Prakash Singh was made minister without election multiple times. SAME RULE AT CENTRE: Article 75(5) — for Union Ministers including PM. RECENT EXAMPLES: Mamata Banerjee (May 2021 — sworn in CM, won Bhabanipur by-election Sept 2021); Yogi Adityanath (Mar 2017 — won UP MLC seat from BJP within months). RAJASTHAN 2003: Vasundhara Raje was MLA before sworn-in; comfortable. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests precise constitutional time limits — high-yield for UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL, RBI Grade B.

questions.stem: The Chief Minister of a state holds office at the:
questions.explanation: Article 164(1): 'The Ministers shall hold office during the PLEASURE of the Governor.' But this 'pleasure' is exercised on the AID AND ADVICE of the Council of Ministers (Art 163), and is constrained by parliamentary democracy norms. EFFECTIVE MEANING: a CM stays in office as long as he/she enjoys the CONFIDENCE of the Legislative Assembly (majority support). If a no-confidence motion passes, CM must resign or recommend dissolution. GOVERNOR'S POSITION: by convention, Governor cannot remove a CM who commands a majority — even in 'pleasure' there's an implicit democratic constraint. POLITICAL CASES: (1) Karnataka 2018 — Governor's invitation to BJP's Yeddyurappa despite Cong-JD(S) alliance majority; SC intervened. (2) Maharashtra 2019 — Fadnavis's pre-dawn swearing-in; resigned within days when majority unclear. SARKARIA COMMISSION (1988) recommended limiting Governor's discretionary powers to prevent partisan abuse. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests the nuance between LEGAL FRAMEWORK ('pleasure') and POLITICAL REALITY ('confidence').

questions.stem: Which article makes it a duty of the CM to communicate cabinet decisions to the Governor?
questions.explanation: Article 167: It is the DUTY of the Chief Minister to: (a) COMMUNICATE to the Governor of the state all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to the administration of the affairs of the state and proposals for legislation. (b) FURNISH such information relating to administration as the Governor may CALL FOR. (c) Submit any matter on which a Minister has decided but the Council has not considered, when so required by the Governor — for consideration by the Council. KEY DUTIES OVERVIEW: (1) Liaison between Governor and Cabinet. (2) Lead Council of Ministers (chair Cabinet meetings). (3) Allocate portfolios. (4) Recommend resignation of any Minister to the Governor. (5) Lead the State in Inter-State Council and NITI Aayog meetings. PARALLEL: Article 78 imposes the SAME duty on the PM vis-à-vis the President. EXAM ANGLE: 'Article 167 = CM's duty' is a UPSC Prelims favourite — appears every 2-3 years. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests precise article-number recall.

questions.stem: Who was the FIRST FEMALE Chief Minister of any Indian state?

options.option_text: J. Jayalalithaa of Tamil Nadu state

questions.explanation: SUCHETA KRIPALANI was the FIRST WOMAN to become CM of an Indian state — she led UTTAR PRADESH from 2 OCTOBER 1963 to 13 March 1967 as a Congress leader. BACKGROUND: born 1908 in Ambala (Punjab); freedom-fighter, educator; member of the Constituent Assembly; sang 'Vande Mataram' in the Assembly on 14 Aug 1947 night. HUSBAND: J.B. Kripalani (Congress President 1946-47). LEGACY: Kripalani is celebrated as a women's rights pioneer; UP Legislature has a portrait of her. SUBSEQUENT FIRSTS: Nandini Satpathy (Odisha, 1972) — second woman CM. Shashikala Kakodkar (Goa, 1973). Anwara Taimur (Assam, 1980). J. Jayalalithaa (Tamil Nadu, 1991). Mayawati (UP, 1995, first Dalit woman CM). Sheila Dikshit (Delhi, 1998 — longest-serving woman CM, 15 years). Mamata Banerjee (West Bengal, 2011). PYQ FREQUENCY: 'first woman CM' appears in CGL, IBPS, RRB GK 2-3× per year. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests significant historical political milestones — high-frequency factual recall.

questions.stem: In a Union Territory, who appoints the Chief Minister where the UT has a Legislative Assembly?

options.option_text: The President of India alone too
The Prime Minister of India alone
The Home Minister of India alone

questions.explanation: UNION TERRITORIES with Legislative Assemblies — Delhi, Puducherry, J&K (post 2019 reorganization) — have a CM appointed by the LIEUTENANT GOVERNOR (LG) or Administrator. The framework is Article 239AA (Delhi-specific) and the Government of UT Act 1963 (for Puducherry). DELHI'S UNIQUE STATUS (NCT-Delhi): Article 239AA gives Delhi a special hybrid status — CM and elected legislature, but key subjects (police, public order, land) remain with LG/Centre. Source of frequent friction (Kejriwal vs LGs of Delhi). 2023-24 Centre-State Acts further empowered LG over services. PUDUCHERRY: smaller UT, similar arrangement. J&K (POST AUG 2019): downgraded from state to UT with legislature; first CM elections held in Oct 2024 (Omar Abdullah). UTs WITHOUT LEGISLATURE: Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep, Chandigarh, Dadra-Nagar-Haveli & Daman-Diu, Ladakh — have an LG/Administrator only, no CM. EXAM ANGLE: 'who appoints CM in UTs' tests federal nuance — comes up in UPSC Prelims and CGL. EXAMINER MINDSET: testing UT vs State distinctions.

questions.stem: What is the MINIMUM AGE qualification to become a Chief Minister of an Indian state?
questions.explanation: Article 173: a person is qualified for the State LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY if 25 YEARS or above. Since the CM must be (or become) a member of the State Legislature, the IMPLICIT minimum age = 25. For LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL membership: 30 years. AGE THRESHOLDS — quick quiz: Lok Sabha MP: 25; Rajya Sabha MP: 30; State LA MLA: 25; State LC MLC: 30; CM: 25 (effectively); PM: 25 (must be LS) or 30 (if RS); President: 35; Vice-President: 35; Governor: 35. YOUNGEST CMs (significant cases): Akhilesh Yadav became UP CM at 38 (2012, then youngest UP CM); Pinarayi Vijayan (Kerala 2016, age 71 — example of older). RECORD: Sashidhar Jadhav (Andhra/Telangana 2014 swearing — different system). VOTER AGE 18 (61st Amendment 1989): voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 — same Constitutional Amendment, but candidacy age 25 unchanged. EXAM ANGLE: 'minimum age for CM' commonly mixes up with President (35) — top-3 confusion in UPSC prep.
